title: Book One · Chapter 163: The Money Stays Home
story:
Leo wants to put a small bowl beside the street game. Visitors could drop coins in it, he says. The children could buy better cards next time.

Ronan looks at the empty space under the drawing of the bowl. He remembers the school's rule. No selling. Would money in a game bowl break that rule? Ronan is not sure. They ask Miss Wu first. They leave the bowl out for now.

She says no bowl. River Street Day is free. Visitors may look and play for free. They must not feel that they should pay. The class may need paper later. They can talk about new paper another time.

Leo crosses the bowl out. He is not very upset. He has many other ideas to work on. Ronan feels glad they have asked. At home he sees his money box. He remembers another idea. He did not tell Leo about it.

He thought he could buy more cards himself. He planned to pay for any extra cards. It would make the game look better. He planned to use some of his bicycle money. He has saved that money for years.

He tells Mum that evening. She is folding the last shirt for its owner.

“Do you need more cards?” she asks.

“We have enough.”

“Then you have your answer.”

“What if enough looks small?”

She sets the shirt down. “Small things can fill a small room.”

Dad comes in while they are talking. Ronan shows him the unused space on the plan. “Where will visitors stand?” Dad asks. Ronan puts his finger in that space.

“Then it already has a job,” Dad says.

Ronan looks at the money box. They already have enough cards to play the game. He can feel proud of the game already. The empty space is for visitors to stand in.

On a free afternoon he walks with his parents. They pass a shop with used bicycles. They stop outside only to look. Dad points to the bicycles. There are large ones and small ones. Some have high seats. One has a low frame and worn handles. Another looks bright but has a bent part near the back.

“Can we choose?” Ronan asks.

“Another day,” Mum says. “We said after the school afternoon, when we have time to check properly.”

“When are you usually open?” Dad asks the man inside. He does not ask him to hold a particular bike. The man may sell these bicycles before they return. Other used bikes may be there next time.

Ronan looks once more, then walks on. He is disappointed for a few steps. “How can I find the right size?” he asks. “You must try the bike first,” Dad says. Can he stop and put his feet down safely? They must check the brakes and wheels too. Then they can talk about the price.

At home the birthday envelope stays with Mum. Ronan's money stays in his box. The clean budget sheet lies between them on the shelf. They have not put money into the school game. They have not bought any bicycle yet. The money is still there for the right bike.

He presses his bell once. Then he puts it back. “Dinner is not ready,” Mum calls from the kitchen. He tells her it is a bicycle bell. She says she has heard that before. He smiles at the old joke and goes to help set out the bowls.

---

重点表达：free＝免费；budget＝预算；brakes＝刹车。

情节提示：frame＝车架；bent＝弯曲的；brakes＝刹车。

理解：1. 为什么不设置收钱的小碗？2. 这次路过自行车店有没有选车或预订？
